title: The health-probe interval is a per-environment durable setting the scheduler honours
description: Split from task-6ec875f4 DoD 5 by governor ruling (20:10Z), on worker-f78e0703's measured finding (16:48Z): composition:579 registers ONE monitoring/health-probes job at the default 60 s and re-registers it at boot, ring.ts:223 probes every environment per tick, the options carry no interval map; child task-cc05c473 is DONE with 'default 60 s only' and is NOT reopened. Per-environment intervals are therefore not a production setting today; this row adds the setting. task-6ec875f4 certifies the shipped default-interval behaviour only.
definitionOfDone: An operator command writes a per-environment probe interval as a durable record (bounded: min/max asserted; refusal code + layer for out-of-range or unknown environment), read through a store port; default 60 s when unset.

The scheduler honours it: two environments with different intervals are probed at their own rates in a fake-clock test (assert probe counts per environment over a window), and a change takes effect without a daemon restart.
Boot re-registration honours the stored intervals - no overwrite back to the default and no double schedule after restart (probe RATE equal before/after, per environment).
The existing health read (`/deployments/health/read` once task-509c6c16 lands, else the current read) discloses the effective interval per environment and the browser exact decoder preserves it.
Fresh focused daemon tests + typecheck with nonzero counts; named broader gates disclosed per lease rules (`full-suite-gate`); physical .js bridges for any new runtime module.

implementationPlan.description:
RE-MEASURE THE THREE FACTS THIS PLAN RESTS ON, BEFORE ANY EDIT. Record each command and its output; a task description's claims are stale by default.

- `sed -n '86,96p;135,145p' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/durable-schedule.ts` — confirm `register` persists at `:93` (`if (this.read().get(id) !== intervalMs) this.persist(id, intervalMs)`) and that `restore` re-arms each persisted id at its STORED interval via `resolve(id)`.
- `git grep -n "HEALTH_PROBE_JOB_ID" -- apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts` — confirm composition `:670` (resolver) and `:672` (`schedules.register(HEALTH_PROBE_JOB_ID, healthProbe)` with NO interval, hence the 60 s default).
- `sed -n '218,236p' apps/daemon/src/monitoring/health-probe-ring.ts` — confirm `createHealthProbeJob` loops `readDeployLedger(...).keys()` inside ONE tick.

THEN REPRODUCE THE DoD 3 DEFECT AS A FAILING ARM FIRST, so the fix has something to turn green: register a job at a non-default interval, persist it, simulate a boot re-registration the way composition does (`register(id, cb)` with no interval), and show the stored interval reverts to 60000. Quote the failing line. This is the row's core defect and it must be seen red before it is fixed.

Also confirm the split children exist and depend on this row (task-749e585a, task-620fb461) so nothing here duplicates them. No files change in this step.

LAND THE DURABLE INTERVAL RECORD (DoD 1's half that this row keeps) as a new module `apps/daemon/src/monitoring/probe-interval-record.ts`, plus its one-line bridge `probe-interval-record.js` containing exactly `export * from "./probe-interval-record.ts";` — the convention `health-probe-contracts.js` already follows, and DoD 5 requires it or plain node cannot load the module.

SURFACE: a store port that reads and writes a per-environment interval, and resolves the EFFECTIVE value — the stored one when set, 60000 when unset. Keep the default in ONE place and export it; both the scheduler (step 4) and child task-620fb461's read will consume it, so a second copy would be a second source of truth.

BOUNDS AND REFUSALS ARE THIS ROW'S TO DEFINE and must be TIGHTER than the scheduler's `validInterval` (integer, >0, <=2_147_483_647 at durable-schedule.ts:32). Choose a defensible operational min and max (a probe interval below a few seconds is a self-inflicted load generator; above an hour it is not monitoring), state the reasoning in a comment at the site, and refuse out-of-range and unknown-environment each with a STABLE CODE AND A ROSTERED LAYER.

Do NOT widen `ScheduleCode` (durable-schedule.ts:16-18) and do NOT introduce a new `*_LAYER` constant — the scheduler's closed union is about scheduling faults; a bad interval is this module's fault. Validate the environment against the same admission the deployment side uses (`admitEnvironmentName`) rather than a fresh regex, so the two cannot drift.

Keep the module under the 250-line target.

TESTS FOR THE RECORD in a new `apps/daemon/src/monitoring/probe-interval-record.test.ts`. Every arm pins a reason code AND the layer that refused (global rail: asserting only "refused" is one added layer away from vacuous).

ARMS:
(a) An unset environment resolves to the 60000 default — assert against the exported constant, not a retyped literal.
(b) A written interval reads back by value, and a SECOND environment's value is independent (write two, read both) — a single-environment arm passes against a store that keeps one global value.
(c) Below-min and above-max each refuse with their code AND layer. Include the exact boundary values on both sides: min-1 refuses, min is accepted, max is accepted, max+1 refuses. An off-by-one at a bound is the defect this arm exists to catch.
(d) Non-integer, NaN, Infinity and negative values refuse with the same code — `validInterval` upstream would also catch some of these, so assert THIS module answers first, or the arm silently becomes a test of the scheduler.
(e) An unknown / malformed environment name refuses with its own code AND layer.
(f) A rewrite replaces rather than accumulates — write, rewrite, read back the second value.

DRILL: for each refusal arm, mutate the production guard and confirm the arm reds; restore and prove with `git diff` for tracked paths. For the two NEW files, `git status --porcelain` them first and prove restoration by SHA256 against a %TEMP% backup in a SEPARATE call — `git diff` is blind to untracked paths and would certify nothing.

GIVE EACH ENVIRONMENT ITS OWN SCHEDULE JOB (DoD 2's production half). Two small edits, no new scheduler.

`apps/daemon/src/monitoring/health-probe-contracts.ts`: add a helper deriving the per-environment job id from `HEALTH_PROBE_JOB_ID`, e.g. `monitoring/health-probes/<environment>`. MEASURED SAFE: `validId` (durable-schedule.ts:34) is `/^[\w./:-]{1,200}$/` and environment names are `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}`, so the composed id already passes — change no guard. Keep `HEALTH_PROBE_JOB_ID` exported unchanged: task-6ec875f4 is WORKING and its arms reference it.

`apps/daemon/src/monitoring/health-probe-ring.ts`: add a per-environment job factory beside `createHealthProbeJob` — the same body without the `for (const environment of readDeployLedger(...).keys())` loop, probing the single environment it was built for. Reuse `probeEnvironment` and the existing ring; do not duplicate the ring construction or the abort handling. Leave `createHealthProbeJob` in place and working: it is what task-6ec875f4 certifies, and removing it would reopen a row this one must not touch.

The scheduler needs no change at all — `register(id, cb, intervalMs)` already persists per id, `arm()` :77 already dedups an unchanged interval, and `restore()` :137-142 already re-arms at the stored value.

COMPOSITION: REGISTER PER ENVIRONMENT AND STOP THE BOOT OVERWRITE (DoD 3). In `apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts`, around `:632` / `:670` / `:672`.

THE DEFECT, restated so it is not 'fixed' vacuously: `:672` calls `schedules.register(HEALTH_PROBE_JOB_ID, healthProbe)` with no interval, so it takes `DEFAULT_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_MS`, and `register` at `durable-schedule.ts:93` then persists that default OVER any stored value — every boot resets an operator's 30 s back to 60 s.

TWO CHANGES:
1. The resolver at `:670` currently answers only `id === HEALTH_PROBE_JOB_ID`. Make it resolve a per-environment id to that environment's job, so `restore()` can re-arm persisted ids after a restart. An unresolvable id already refuses `SCHEDULE_TARGET_UNRESOLVED` and is dropped (`:139-141`) — keep that behaviour for genuinely unknown ids rather than manufacturing a callback.
2. Register each environment at its EFFECTIVE interval read from the step-2 port — read the stored value FIRST and pass it, so the persisted value is re-persisted unchanged rather than clobbered. An environment with no stored interval registers at the 60000 default, which is correct and must stay correct.

Boot ORDER matters: if composition registers before reading the record, the default is already persisted and the read is too late. State the order in a comment at the site.

An environment appearing for the first time between boots must still get a schedule at the default — do not make registration conditional on a stored record existing.

THE FAKE-CLOCK SCHEDULER TEST (DoD 2 and DoD 3) in a new `apps/daemon/src/monitoring/health-probe-schedule.test.ts`. Inject `ScheduleConfig.timer` (durable-schedule.ts:9-15) — a `ScheduleTimer` whose `set(tick, intervalMs)` records the id's armed interval and hands back a handle you drive manually, and whose `clear(handle)` records the release. `now` is injectable too. No real timers, no wall-clock waiting.

ARMS:
(a) DIFFERENT RATES: two environments with different stored intervals, driven over the same window, are probed at their OWN rates — assert PROBE COUNTS PER ENVIRONMENT, not merely the intervals the timer was asked for. `set()`'s argument proves what was requested; the DoD asks what actually happened. A one-environment version of this arm is vacuous.
(b) A CHANGE TAKES EFFECT WITHOUT A RESTART: write a new interval through the port, re-register, and assert the environment's probe count over the next window follows the NEW rate while the other environment's is unchanged.
(c) BOOT RE-REGISTRATION, the defect from step 1: record each environment's armed interval and the persisted record, simulate the boot path, and assert the stored interval is BYTE-UNCHANGED and the rate is EQUAL before and after — per environment. This is the arm that was red in step 1.
(d) NO DOUBLE SCHEDULE: after a restart, exactly one live handle exists per environment. Assert from the timer's own ledger of `set` minus `clear`, not from a count of registrations.
(e) A NEWLY APPEARED environment with no stored record is scheduled at the 60000 default.

TEARDOWN (DoD 5, epic rail 4): release the schedule in a `finally` and assert the injected timer's `clear` was called for EVERY handle it created — a leaked interval makes every later gate on this board inadmissible. Assert it; do not assume it.

DRILL (c) and (a): revert the composition fix and confirm (c) reds; make both environments share one job id and confirm (a) reds. Restore each and prove it.

GATES (DoD 5), ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (Skill `adversarial-self-review`), AND PATH DECLARATION.

Run the focused legs first and quote their `Test Files N passed` count lines — exit 0 is not evidence, and a filter matching nothing also exits 0:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (the row's owning package leg).
- `pnpm typecheck` — EXIT 0 with a planted-error control in a NEW file to prove the leg is not short-circuiting; delete the planted file and show the clean re-run.
Acquire `full-suite-gate` for the full daemon leg (one full suite at a time on this host), announce GATE START/END with the UTC window, and release on EVERY exit path including failure. Every drill in steps 3-6 happens OUTSIDE the lease — they mutate shared files on disk. The root lane covers no `apps/**` file, so do not quote a bare root `pnpm test` count line as evidence here.

VERIFY THE BRIDGE ACTUALLY LOADS: run plain `node` against the new `.js` bridge and confirm it resolves the module's exports. A bridge that exists but does not load satisfies a grep and nothing else.

CONFIRM THE SIBLING IS UNDISTURBED: task-6ec875f4 is WORKING and certifies the shipped default-interval behaviour. Its arms must be green and UNEDITED — `git diff` its files and show no change. If one of its arms contradicts per-environment job ids, STOP and report rather than editing it.

Adversarial pass: does the boot path read the stored interval BEFORE registering, or is the default already persisted by then? If two environments share a stored interval, does the dedup at `arm()` collapse them into one job? What happens when an environment is removed from the deploy ledger between boots — is its persisted record orphaned forever? Does any test leave an interval armed? Is any drilled mutation still on disk (`git diff` every production file you touched, and SHA256 every untracked one against its %TEMP% backup)?

Declare EXACTLY the files changed via complete_step.modifiedFiles / moe.declare_files. Do not touch the two children's paths (task-749e585a: runtime-vocabulary and the digest mirrors; task-620fb461: the health read and the browser client).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED — keeping one job id and teaching `createHealthProbeJob` to skip environments whose interval has not elapsed. It reimplements scheduling inside the callback, makes the effective rate a function of the shared tick (so a 30 s environment under a 60 s tick silently stays at 60 s), and leaves `DurableSchedule`'s persistence, dedup and restore doing nothing for it. One job id per environment reuses machinery that is already proven and already restart-safe.

REJECTED — a second scheduler or an interval map threaded through `HealthProbeOptions`. `durable-schedule.ts` already stores a per-id interval durably; a parallel map would be a second source of truth for the same fact, and DoD 3's restart property would then have to be proven twice.

REJECTED — widening `ScheduleCode` or adding a `*_LAYER` constant for the record's refusals. The scheduler's closed union is about scheduling faults; a bad interval or unknown environment is the record's fault and belongs to the new module under a rostered layer.

REJECTED — planning the operator command and the health read in this row. Measured ~25 files against the 20-file cap, and the three responsibilities are genuinely separable. Split into task-749e585a and task-620fb461, both depending on this row, which is the leaf (PLAN IN BUILD ORDER rail).

REJECTED — changing `validId` to admit the composed job id. Measured: `/^[\w./:-]{1,200}$/` already admits `monitoring/health-probes/staging`. Verify before assuming otherwise.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED by architect-5ac70ba8 2026-09-07 13:10-13:25Z at HEAD on moe/work-2026-09-04.

THIS ROW WAS SPLIT. See row comment-074d042d for the full DoD redistribution: this row keeps DoD 1's DURABLE RECORD half, DoD 2 and DoD 3; task-749e585a takes DoD 1's command surface; task-620fb461 takes DoD 4. Both children carry parentTaskId and dependsOn this row. This row's dependsOn stays EMPTY and that is correct — it is the LEAF, and pointing it at its own children would close a cycle.

THE DESCRIPTION'S PREMISE IS TRUE AND I RE-MEASURED IT. `apps/daemon/src/monitoring/health-probe-contracts.ts:6` — `HEALTH_PROBE_JOB_ID = "monitoring/health-probes"`, ONE id. `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:632` builds one `createHealthProbeJob(...)`, `:670` resolves `id === HEALTH_PROBE_JOB_ID ? healthProbe : …`, `:672` registers it. `health-probe-ring.ts:218-235 createHealthProbeJob` loops `for (const environment of readDeployLedger(store, projectId).keys())` INSIDE one tick, so every environment is probed at one shared rate. No interval map anywhere.

THE DURABLE PER-INTERVAL MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS — THIS IS THE FINDING THAT MAKES THE ROW SMALL. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/durable-schedule.ts` (163 lines) is keyed by job id with a PER-ID interval that is already persisted and already restart-safe:
- `register(id, callback, intervalMs = DEFAULT_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_MS)` :88;
- `persist(id, intervalMs)` :118-119 writes `{id, intervalMs}` as event `moe.durable-schedule.registered`;
- `arm()` :74-82 — `if (old?.intervalMs === intervalMs) return OK`, which is the no-double-schedule guard;
- `restore()` :135-142 reads the persisted map and re-arms each id AT ITS STORED INTERVAL via `resolve(id)`.
So DoD 2's "different rates" and DoD 3's "no double schedule" are mostly ALREADY BUILT. The work is to give each environment its own job id and to stop the boot path clobbering the stored value. Do NOT write a second scheduler.

THE DoD 3 DEFECT IS REAL, MEASURED, AND ONE LINE. `composition:672` calls `schedules.register(HEALTH_PROBE_JOB_ID, healthProbe)` with NO interval argument, so it takes `DEFAULT_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000` (:3). `register` then runs `:93 if (this.read().get(id) !== intervalMs) this.persist(id, intervalMs)` — which OVERWRITES a stored 30 s back to 60 s on EVERY boot. That is exactly DoD 3's "no overwrite back to the default", and it is a live defect today, not a hypothetical.

JOB IDS COMPOSE SAFELY. `validId` (durable-schedule.ts:34) is `/^[\w./:-]{1,200}$/`, and environment names are admitted by `admitEnvironmentName` as `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}`. So `monitoring/health-probes/<environment>` is a valid id under the existing guard — no guard change is owed. `validInterval` (:32) is integer, > 0, <= 2_147_483_647; the row's own min/max bounds must be TIGHTER and are this row's to define.

THE FAKE CLOCK SEAM ALREADY EXISTS. `ScheduleConfig.timer?: ScheduleTimer` (:9-15) with `set(tick, intervalMs)` / `clear(handle)`; `nodeTimer` (:27-30) is only the default. A test injects its own timer, records the intervalMs each id was armed with, and drives ticks by hand — that is how DoD 2's "probe counts per environment over a window" is asserted without real time. `now?: () => number` is injectable too.

REFUSAL VOCABULARY TO REUSE, NOT EXTEND. `ScheduleRefusal` (:19-24) is `{ok:false, id, code, layer:"DAEMON_INGRESS"}` over a closed `ScheduleCode` union (:16-18). The interval RECORD's own refusals (out-of-range, unknown environment) belong to this row's new module with its own code+layer; do not widen `ScheduleCode` and do not introduce a new `*_LAYER` constant — reuse a rostered layer.

`.js` BRIDGES ARE THE CONVENTION IN THIS DIRECTORY AND DoD 5 REQUIRES ONE. `apps/daemon/src/monitoring/health-probe-contracts.js` is exactly one line: `export * from "./health-probe-contracts.ts";`. `health-probe-ring.js` exists likewise. A new runtime module without its bridge cannot be loaded by plain node.

SIBLING STATE: task-e651725c (the durable schedule) and task-cc05c473 (ring/UP-DEGRADED-DOWN) are both DONE and landed; task-509c6c16 (`/deployments/health/read`) is DONE. task-6ec875f4 is WORKING and certifies the shipped DEFAULT-interval behaviour only — it is explicitly NOT reopened by this row, so do not touch its arms.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE BOOT OVERWRITE IS THE WHOLE OF DoD 3 AND IT IS EASY TO 'FIX' VACUOUSLY. Passing the stored interval back into `register()` at boot only works if the stored value is read FIRST; if composition reads it after registering, the default has already been persisted. Prefer letting `restore()` own re-arming and having composition register only what is absent — and assert the stored value is UNCHANGED across a simulated restart, not merely that the rate looks right afterwards.
2. A RATE ASSERTION THAT NEVER SEES A SECOND RATE IS VACUOUS. Two environments must have DIFFERENT intervals in the same test, and the counts must be asserted per environment over the same window. A test with one environment passes against a scheduler that ignores the record entirely.
3. DO NOT ASSERT THE RATE FROM THE INJECTED TIMER'S ARGUMENT ALONE. `set(tick, intervalMs)` tells you what was REQUESTED; the DoD asks for probe COUNTS per environment. Drive ticks and count actual probes per environment, then optionally corroborate with the armed interval.
4. LEAKED TIMERS BREAK EVERY LATER GATE ON THIS BOARD (epic rail 4). `DurableSchedule` has a release path; every test that registers must release in a `finally`, and the injected timer's `clear` must be observed to have been called for every handle it created. Assert that, do not assume it.
5. `readDeployLedger(...).keys()` is the environment source today. A per-environment registration must handle an environment appearing or disappearing between boots — `restore()` :136 already drops armed ids absent from the persisted map, but a NEW environment with no stored interval must still get the 60 s default rather than no schedule at all. Assert the newly-appeared case.
6. DO NOT REOPEN task-6ec875f4's ARMS. It is WORKING and certifies the shipped default-interval behaviour; its assertions must stay green unchanged. If an arm there contradicts per-environment ids, STOP and report rather than editing it.
7. A new runtime module without its one-line `.js` bridge cannot be loaded by plain node (DoD 5). Add it in the same step as the module, not at the end.
8. Shared checkout: `git status --porcelain` the owned paths before editing; never revert, stash or commit a foreign path.
